newsitem.title: USA: CBOT corn closes lower on soy drop, weather.
newsitem.headline: CBOT corn closes lower on soy drop, weather.

text.p: CBOT corn futures closed lower on a drop in soybean futures and on overall good crop weather in the U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Warmer temperatures and plentiful soil moisture in the Midwest were helping to boost corn production prospects, the traders said.
Improving crop condition ratings also were cited as USDA Monday boosted ratings for U.S. corn as of Sunday to 65 percent good to excellent, above 60 percent in that category the previous week.
But the corn market showed resiliency and held firm early.
The gains in early dealings were linked to a rebound from the sharp break in early trading Monday, a break which was tied to a steep slide in soybeans.

Corn futures also were underpinned by Monday's National Weather Service six- to 10-day outlook for below normal temperatures through much of the Midwest from Saturday through Wednesday. The corn crop needs warmer weather to develop properly and to enhance production prospects, traders said.
Corn closed 1/2 to 2-1/2 cents per bushel lower, with July down 2-1/4 at $2.71-3/4 a bushel.
ABN Amro-Chicago Corp bought 13.0 million bushels of July and 12.0 million December, traders said.
Cargill Inc sold three million July, Refco Inc sold eight million December and Farmers Commodities Corp sold four million bushels of December, traders said.
Corn futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 57,000 contracts, below the 59,202 traded Monday.

In corn options, Prudential Securities sold 400 July $3.00 calls at 3/8 cent, Rand Financial sold 200 September $2.70 calls at 10 cents and ABN Amro sold 200 July $2.80 calls at 2-1/2 cents, traders said.
Corn options volume was estimated at 13,000 contracts, above the 12,309 traded Monday.
